headline: Endorsed an ANR plan, accepted a withdrawal, and approved a preliminary subdivision plan with comments, all 5-0.
summary: The board endorsed a Subdivision Approval Not Required plan for 0 Brookwood Road, accepted an applicant's request to withdraw a special permit for 371 Cabot Street without prejudice, and approved a preliminary subdivision plan for 115 Cross Lane with several comments to the applicant. The board also tabled election of 2026 officers and signatory authorization to March 10, 2026, and approved the January 13, 2026 minutes as amended.
decisions: Endorsed the Subdivision Approval Not Required Plan for 0 Brookwood Road, applicant Walter Theodore Miller, 5-0.
Accepted the applicant's request to withdraw Special Permit #204-25 for 371 Cabot Street without prejudice, 5-0.
Approved the Preliminary Plan of Subdivision for 115 Cross Lane, applicant Merrill Nearis, with three comments, 5-0.
Tabled the Election of 2026 Planning Board Chairperson and Vice-Chairperson to March 10, 2026, 5-0.
Tabled Authorization of Planning Board Signatory to March 10, 2026, 5-0.
Approved the January 13, 2026 meeting minutes as amended, 5-0.

4.    Preliminary Plan of Subdivision – 115 Cross Lane – Merrill Nearis 48 
 a. Plan shows a private minor subdivision roadway creating two (2) additional  49 
  residential parcels on a 1.84 parcel in an R22 zoning district for a total of  50 
  three (3) residential parcels. The private right-of-way will be 40 feet wide,  51 
  173 feet long, with a 100 foot diameter cul-de-sac. The paved roadway will be 52 
  24 feet wide with a bituminous curb and a hammerhead turning area. 53 
 54 
Bob Griffin on behalf of the applicant, explained that this parcel is 1.8 acres of land on Cross 55 
Lane. Behind the property is a small OSRD subdivision, built in approximately 2017. There is 56 
also a gravel parking lot across the street from the property. The existing Cross Lane is 57 
approximately 24’ wide of pavement and striped. There is also a new sidewalk on the righthand 58 
side. There is an existing ranch style house on the lot, with an open area behind the house. The 59 
site shows no significant topographical changes and excellent sight distance in both directions. 60 
There is an existing drain line which runs left to right across the bottom of the plan and a nearby 61 
manhole. There are no records available at the City Engineering Department indicating the 62 
ownership of the pipe or when it was installed. The owner of the property states that there was a 63 
golf course in the area at one time and the drain may be associated with that use.  64 
 65 
Griffin explained that the proposal is for a minor subdivision. The plan shows a private right-of-66 
way which will be 40’ wide, 173’ long, with a 100’ diameter cul-de-sac. The paved roadway will 67 
be 24’ wide with a bituminous concrete curb and hammerhead turn-around area. The Zone 68 
requires 22,000 s.f. of land and 150’ of frontage and each of the lots exceeds that. In terms of the 69 
road construction, a hammerhead turning area is proposed. From a grading standpoint, the goal is 70 
to install a high point at the middle of the length of the road to help push water back towards 71 
Cross Lane. There is a catch basin at the end of the hammerhead turning area which will pick up 72 
the water, pretreat it, and allow it to flow into infiltration basins underneath the road. The 73 
stormwater management standards require no increase in the rate or volume of runoff. Infiltration 74 
devices, such as drywells, are shown on the plan next to the homes with the intention of handling 75 
any excess runoff from the houses. In order to keep the water and sewer utilities the correct 76 
distance apart, a minor easement is proposed for the sewer line. A single water line will be 77 
brought to each house. The grades will be lifted a bit to make sure there are no wet basement 78 
issues for the houses. The road construction standards for a minor subdivision include a 12’ 79 
travel lane on each side and a 40’ wide right of way. The applicant is interested in reducing the 80 
construction a bit. It is believed that three houses could be managed around 20’ of pavement 81 
instead. The proposal is to potentially reduce the width of the right of way to allow more 82 
flexibility for the house footprints. In terms of the amount of soil required to provide the 83 
intended grade, the applicant plans to bring in approximately 5,000 cubic yards of granular fill to 84 
raise up the area.  85 
 86 
Griffin stated that the applicant is requesting six waivers. The first one is for a hammerhead 87 
instead of a round cul-de-sac. This is proposed due to the small number of houses. Clawson 88 
noted that this waiver may not be necessary. Griffin explained that the second waiver request is 89 
for 10’ wide utilities. The applicant plans to keep the water and sewer lines the correct distances 90
